title: 1973 AHSME Problem 33
statement: When one ounce of water is added to a mixture of acid and water, the new mixture is \(20\%\) acid. When one ounce of acid is added to the new mixture, the result is \(33\frac13\%\) acid. The percentage of acid in the original mixture is

solutions.text:
Let the original mixture contain \(x\) ounces of water and \(y\) ounces of acid. The two additions give \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{y}{x+y+1}&=\frac15,\\ \frac{y+1}{x+y+2}&=\frac13. \end{aligned} \] These simplify to \[ x+1=4y, \qquad x=2y+1. \] Hence \(y=1\) and \(x=3.\) The original acid percentage was \[ 100\cdot\frac{y}{x+y} =100\cdot\frac14=25\%. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let \(x\) and \(y\) be the original ounces of water and acid
Write one concentration equation after adding water and another after subsequently adding acid
